argentinosaurus:eswiki:12.title: Argentinosaurus huinculensis (Crecimiento y patrones de reproducción)

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Albian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous (Albian),

facts.statement: The first bone of Argentinosaurus was discovered in 1987 by a farmer near Plaza Huincul, Argentina.
facts.quote: The first Argentinosaurus bone was discovered in 1987 by a farmer on his farm near the city of Plaza Huincul.

facts.statement: A scientific excavation led by José Bonaparte in 1989 yielded back vertebrae and parts of a sacrum from the site.
facts.quote: A scientific excavation of the site led by the Argentine palaeontologist José Bonaparte was conducted in 1989, yielding several back vertebrae and parts of a sacrum

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus was formally named by José Bonaparte and Rodolfo Coria in 1993.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus was named by Bonaparte and the Argentine palaeontologist Rodolfo Coria in 1993

facts.statement: Guillermo Heredia discovered the first bone, now identified as a fibula, in 1987 on his farm 8 km east of Plaza Huincul in Neuquén Province.
facts.quote: The first Argentinosaurus bone, which is now thought to be a fibula (calf bone), was discovered in 1987 by Guillermo Heredia on his farm "Las Overas" about 8 km east of Plaza Huincul, in Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Argentinosaurus huinculensis is catalogued as MCF-PVPH 1.
facts.quote: The individual, which later became the holotype of Argentinosaurus huinculensis, is catalogued under the specimen number MCF-PVPH 1.

facts.statement: In 1996, a complete but deformed femur from the same locality was assigned to the genus and exhibited at the Museo Carmen Funes.
facts.quote: In 1996, Bonaparte referred (assigned) a complete femur (thigh bone) from the same locality to the genus, which was put on exhibit at the Museo Carmen Funes.

facts.statement: As of 2019, it remained uncertain whether the additional femora found in the region actually belonged to Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: As of 2019, however, it was still uncertain whether any of these femora belonged to Argentinosaurus.

facts.statement: Despite being known only from fragmentary remains, Argentinosaurus is estimated to have been 30 to 35 meters long and weighed 65 to 80 tonnes.
facts.quote: Although it is only known from fragmentary remains, Argentinosaurus was one of the largest known land animals of all time, measuring 30 - 35 m long and weighing 65 - 80 t.

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus is classified as a member of Titanosauria, the dominant sauropod group during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was a member of Titanosauria, the dominant group of sauropods during the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The fragmentary nature of the remains makes interpreting the anatomy of Argentinosaurus difficult.
facts.quote: The fragmentary nature of Argentinosaurus remains makes their interpretation difficult.

facts.statement: In 2023, Paul and Larramendi proposed that the holotype of Argentinosaurus weighed a maximum of 75 to 80 metric tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2023, Paul and Larramendi proposed that the holotype would have weighed between 75 - 80 MT at maximum.

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate among scientists regarding whether Argentinosaurus was the largest known titanosaur.
facts.quote: While Argentinosaurus was definitely a massive animal, there is disagreement over whether it was the largest known titanosaur.

facts.statement: In 2017, Carballido and colleagues argued that Argentinosaurus was smaller than Patagotitan based on vertebral measurements.
facts.quote: In 2017, Carballido and colleagues considered Argentinosaurus to be smaller than Patagotitan, since the latter had a greater area enclosed by the neural spine, diapophyses, and parapophyses of its anterior dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 2019, Paul countered that Argentinosaurus was larger than Patagotitan because of its considerably longer dorsal column.
facts.quote: However, Paul found Patagotitan to be smaller than Argentinosaurus in 2019, due to the latter's dorsal column being considerably longer.

facts.statement: It is debated whether other sauropods like Maraapunisaurus or giant mamenchisaurids might have exceeded Argentinosaurus in size, though evidence for them is scant.
facts.quote: Even if Argentinosaurus was the largest-known titanosaur, other sauropods including Maraapunisaurus and a giant mamenchisaurid, may have been larger, although these are only known from very scant remains.

facts.statement: A reconstructed dorsal vertebra of Argentinosaurus is 159 cm tall and 129 cm wide.
facts.quote: one dorsal vertebra has a reconstructed height of 159 cm and a width of 129 cm

facts.statement: The centra of Argentinosaurus dorsal vertebrae can be up to 57 cm wide.
facts.quote: the vertebral centra are up to 57 cm in width

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of Argentinosaurus were opisthocoelous, meaning they were concave at the rear.
facts.quote: The dorsals were opisthocoelous (concave at the rear) as in other macronarian sauropods

facts.statement: The dorsal ribs of Argentinosaurus were tubular and cylindrical, unlike those of other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The dorsal ribs were tubular and cylindrical in shape, in contrast with other titanosaurs

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus likely had six sacral vertebrae, similar to many other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus, like many titanosaurs, probably had six sacral vertebrae

facts.statement: The complete femur assigned to Argentinosaurus is 2.5 meters long.
facts.quote: The complete femur that was assigned to Argentinosaurus is 2.5 m long

facts.statement: The femoral shaft of Argentinosaurus has a circumference of about 1.18 meters at its narrowest point.
facts.quote: The femoral shaft has a circumference of about 1.18 m at its narrowest part

facts.statement: Mazzetta and colleagues estimated the original length of the Argentinosaurus femur at 2.557 meters.
facts.quote: Mazzetta and colleagues used regression equations to estimate its original length at 2.557 m

facts.statement: In 2019, Paul estimated the original length of the Argentinosaurus femur at 2.575 meters.
facts.quote: later in 2019 Paul gave a similar estimate of 2.575 m

facts.statement: When a slender bone from the Argentinosaurus holotype was identified as a tibia, it was thought to have a short cnemial crest.
facts.quote: When it was identified as a tibia, it was thought to have a comparatively short cnemial crest

facts.statement: The slender bone from the Argentinosaurus holotype lacks tibia proportions and details but resembles sauropod fibulae.
facts.quote: this bone lacks both the proportions and anatomical details of a tibia, while being similar in shape to other sauropod fibulae

facts.statement: Bonaparte and Coria described Argentinosaurus in 1993 and noted its ribs were hollow.
facts.quote: Bonaparte and Coria, in their 1993 description, noted the ribs were hollow

facts.statement: In 1993, two articulated vertebrae were thought to be from the rear of the dorsal column, but later studies interpreted them as the sixth and seventh vertebrae.
facts.quote: In 1993, two articulated (still connected) vertebrae were thought to be of the rear part of the dorsal column but are interpreted as the sixth and seventh vertebrae in the two later studies

facts.statement: One vertebra has been interpreted as the first, fifth, or third vertebra in different studies.
facts.quote: One vertebra was interpreted by these studies as the first, fifth or third

facts.statement: The presence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations in Argentinosaurus is a contentious issue.
facts.quote: Another contentious issue is the presence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations, accessory joints between vertebrae that were located below the main articular processes

facts.statement: Some authors argue that articular structures seen in Argentinosaurus are actually thickened vertebral laminae rather than true hyposphene-hypantrum articulations.
facts.quote: Other authors argued most titanosaur genera lacked hyposphene-hypantrum articulations and that the articular structures seen in Epachthosaurus and Argentinosaurus are thickened vertebral laminae (ridges)

facts.statement: Bonaparte and Coria proposed the family Andesauridae for Argentinosaurus, Andesaurus, and Epachthosaurus.
facts.quote: Bonaparte and Coria proposed a separate family for the three genera, the Andesauridae

facts.statement: The families Titanosauridae and Andesauridae were united into the higher group Titanosauria.
facts.quote: Both families were united into a new, higher group called Titanosauria

facts.statement: A 2003 study found both Titanosauridae and Andesauridae to be invalid families.
facts.quote: A 2003 study by Jeffrey Wilson and Paul Upchurch found both Titanosauridae and Andesauridae to be invalid

facts.statement: In 2004, Upchurch and colleagues introduced the group Lithostrotia for more derived members of Titanosauria.
facts.quote: In 2004, Upchurch and colleagues introduced a new group called Lithostrotia that included the more derived (evolved) members of Titanosauria

facts.statement: In 2007, Calvo and colleagues named the clade Lognkosauria, which includes Futalognkosaurus and Mendozasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2007, Calvo and colleagues named Futalognkosaurus; they found it to form a clade with Mendozasaurus and named it Lognkosauria

facts.statement: A 2017 study recovered Argentinosaurus as a member of Lognkosauria and the sister taxon of Patagotitan.
facts.quote: A 2017 study by Carballido and colleagues recovered Argentinosaurus as a member of Lognkosauria and the sister taxon of Patagotitan

facts.statement: In 2019, Julian Silva Junior and colleagues found Argentinosaurus to belong to Lognkosauria again.
facts.quote: In 2019, Julian Silva Junior and colleagues found Argentinosaurus to belong to Lognkosauria once again

facts.statement: A 2019 study found Argentinosaurus in Lognkosauria, which forms a larger clade with Rinconsauria named Colossosauria.
facts.quote: Another 2019 study by González Riga and colleagues also found Argentinosaurus to belong to Lognkosauria; they found this group to form a larger clade with Rinconsauria within Titanosauria, which they named Colossosauria

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus lived in what is now South America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Sudamérica

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Argentinosaurus were discovered by Guillermo Heredia on a rural estate near Plaza Huincul in Argentine Patagonia.
facts.quote: Sus vestigios óseos fueron descubiertos por Guillermo Heredia, en una estancia rural cerca de Plaza Huincul, en la Patagonia argentina

facts.statement: The fossil material is now housed at the Museo Carmen Funes and the Museo de La Plata.
facts.quote: El material se encuentra ahora bajo el resguardo del Museo Carmen Funes y del Museo de La Plata

facts.statement: The genus Argentinosaurus was named by Bonaparte and Coria in 1993.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bonaparte & Coria, 1993

facts.statement: The species A. huinculensis was named by Bonaparte and Coria in 1993.
facts.quote: species_authority: Bonaparte & Coria, 1993

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus belongs to the family Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: familia: Lognkosauria

facts.statement: Intermediate estimates suggest Argentinosaurus was 33 to 36 meters long and weighed 70 to 80 tonnes.
facts.quote: un margen intermedio y probable estima a Argentinosaurus con 33-36 m de longitud y una masa corporal de 70-80 toneladas

facts.statement: Various studies have estimated Argentinosaurus to be between 30 and 39.7 meters long and weigh between 55 and 90 tonnes.
facts.quote: Diferentes estudios, a lo largo de los años, han estimado su tamaño en un rango de entre 30 a 39,7 m de longitud, con un peso de 55 a 90 tn

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus could reach a height of more than 16 meters when stretching its neck upward.
facts.quote: y una altura de más de 16 metros al erguir el cuello

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus had simple, long, thin, tube-shaped dental batteries adapted for cutting vegetation.
facts.quote: provista de simples pero largas coronas dentarias, delgadas y en forma de tubo

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus had a robust, muscular torso supported by four massive, cylindrical legs.
facts.quote: Su torso debió haber sido robusto y musculoso, para alojar sus enormes órganos internos, y sostenido por cuatro patas macizas y cilíndricas

facts.statement: In 2016, Mark Hallett and Matthew Wedel estimated that Argentinosaurus eggs were likely only 1 liter in volume.
facts.quote: In 2016, Mark Hallett and Matthew Wedel stated that the eggs of Argentinosaurus were probably only 1 L in volume

facts.statement: Hallett and Wedel estimated that a newly hatched Argentinosaurus was no longer than 1 meter and weighed no more than 5 kilograms.
facts.quote: and that a hatched Argentinosaurus was no longer than 1 m and not heavier than 5 kg

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus may have been preyed upon by Mapusaurus, one of the largest known theropods.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus might have been preyed on by Mapusaurus, which is among the largest theropods known

facts.statement: Mapusaurus fossils found together suggest it may have hunted in packs to take down large prey like Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus is known from at least seven individuals found together, raising the possibility that this theropod hunted in packs to bring down large prey including Argentinosaurus

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation consists of yellowish and greenish fine-to-medium grain sandstones, some containing volcanic ash.
facts.quote: The Huincul Formation is composed of yellowish and greenish sandstones of fine-to-medium grain, some of which are tuffaceous

facts.statement: The deposits containing Argentinosaurus were laid down during the Lower Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: These deposits were laid down during the Lower Cretaceous

facts.statement: Fossilized pollen indicates a wide variety of plants, including ferns, gymnosperms, and angiosperms, lived in the Huincul Formation environment.
facts.quote: Fossilised pollen indicates a wide variety of plants were present in the Huincul Formation

facts.statement: Other sauropods found in the same formation include the titanosaur Choconsaurus and rebbachisaurids like Cathartesaura and Limaysaurus.
facts.quote: In addition to Argentinosaurus, the sauropods of the Huincul Formation are represented by another titanosaur, Choconsaurus, and several rebbachisaurids including Cathartesaura, Limaysaurus, and some unnamed species

facts.statement: Theropods discovered in the same formation include Mapusaurus, Skorpiovenator, Huinculsaurus, Overoraptor, Aoniraptor, and Gualicho.
facts.quote: Theropods including carcharodontosaurids such as Mapusaurus, abelisaurids including Skorpiovenator, Ilokelesia, and Tralkasaurus, noasaurids such as Huinculsaurus, paravians such as Overoraptor, and other theropods such as Aoniraptor and Gualicho have also been discovered there

facts.statement: Computer simulations determined that Argentinosaurus walked using a gait close to a pace, where limbs on the same side moved simultaneously.
facts.quote: The optimal gait found by the algorithms was close to a pace (forelimb and hind limb on the same side of the body move simultaneously)

facts.statement: The computer model estimated a top speed of just over 2 meters per second (7.2 km/h or 5 mph) for Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: The model reached a top speed of just over 2 m/s (7.2 km/h, 5 mph)

facts.statement: Researchers cautioned that the computer model of Argentinosaurus is not fully realistic and too simplistic.
facts.quote: The authors of the study cautioned the model is not fully realistic and too simplistic, and that it could be improved in many areas

facts.statement: It is suggested that Argentinosaurus might have been preyed on by Mapusaurus.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus might have been preyed on by Mapusaurus

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Argentinosaurus are very incomplete, consisting of only a few vertebrae, a fibula, fragmentary ribs, and the sacrum.
facts.quote: No se ha recuperado mucho de Argentinosaurus, apenas algunas vértebras, un peroné, costillas fragmentarias y el sacro.

facts.statement: Six dorsal vertebrae were described in detail, with the largest measuring 1.59 meters high and 1.29 meters wide.
facts.quote: Seis vértebras dorsales fueran descritas detalladamente, la mayor de ellas alcanzando un tamaño de 1,59 m de alto con 1,29 m de ancho.

facts.statement: The sacral bone tissue displays large macrocysts separated by very thin bone laminae.
facts.quote: El tejido óseo del sacro exhibe además macroceldas de gran tamaño y separadas entre sí por láminas óseas muy delgadas.

facts.statement: Because relatives possessed defensive osteoderms on their backs, researchers hypothesize that Argentinosaurus may have had similar structures.
facts.quote: Los parientes de esta criatura presentaban placas óseas en la espalda, llamadas osteodermos, que funcionaban como una armadura defensiva, por eso se piensa que Argentinosaurus también podía tener estas estructuras.

facts.statement: An incomplete femur attributed to the same specimen measures approximately 1.18 meters.
facts.quote: Este eje femoral es de alrededor de 1,18 metros.

facts.statement: The original authors estimated the total length of the femur to be no less than 240 centimeters.
facts.quote: Según los autores originales su tamaño no debió ser menor a los 240 cm.

facts.statement: In 1996, paleontologist José Bonaparte estimated the femur length at 250 centimeters.
facts.quote: Posteriormente en 1996, fue el paleontólogo José Bonaparte quien estimó al fémur en 250 cm de largo.

facts.statement: Mazzetta and colleagues estimated the femur length at 255.7 centimeters.
facts.quote: Similar al tamaño calculado por Mazzetta et al., quienes lo estimaron en 255,7 cm de longitud.

facts.statement: The fused sacral vertebrae measure 1.2 meters in total and anatomical features confirm the absence of a sixth vertebra.
facts.quote: Juntos el fósil mide 1,2 m; y a raíz de sus características anatómicas, se demuestra la falta de una sexta.

facts.statement: An early reconstruction by Gregory S. Paul estimated Argentinosaurus to be between 30 and 35 meters long and weigh between 80 and 100 tons.
facts.quote: Una temprana reconstrucción de Gregory S. Paul estimó que Argentinosaurus midió entre 30 y 35 metros de longitud y que pesó de 80 a 100 toneladas.

facts.statement: A later publication in Current Science proposed a maximum estimate of 45 meters in length and 100 tons in weight.
facts.quote: Unos años más tarde, en una publicación de la revista Current Science, se le apunta con un estimado, máximo y liberal, de 45 metros y 100 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: Mazzetta and colleagues used regression equations based on femur anatomy to estimate an average weight of 73 tons, with a possible range of 60 to 88 tons.
facts.quote: Mazzetta y colaboradores utilizan ecuaciones de regresión, con datos extraídos de la anatomía del fémur (hueso clave en el soporte del peso del animal), y promedian un peso estimado de 73 toneladas, y ofrecen un amplio rango que va de 60 a 88 toneladas como su posible masa corporal.

facts.statement: In 2008, Jorge Calvo and colleagues revised titanosaur size estimates, calculating Argentinosaurus to be 33 meters long.
facts.quote: En 2008, Jorge Calvo y colegas realizan una revisión de los tamaños estimados de titanosaurios, calculando a Argentinosaurus con 33 metros de largo.

facts.statement: A volumetric reconstruction displayed at the Carmen Funes Municipal Museum depicts the animal as 39.7 meters long, 7.3 meters high at the shoulders, and weighing 83.2 tons.
facts.quote: Una reconstrucción de su esqueleto, montado y expuesto en el Museo municipal Carmen Funes, muestra al coloso titanosaurio con 39,7 metros de longitud, una altura de 7,3 metros hasta la zona de los hombros y una masa corporal de 83,2 toneladas, a partir de una estimación volumétrica.

facts.statement: In 2023, Gregory Paul and Asier Larramendi updated their reconstruction to estimate a mass of 75–80 tons, using new anatomical data from close relatives Dreadnoughtus and Patagotitan.
facts.quote: En 2023, Gregory Paul, con Asier Larramendi, actualizaron su reconstrucción de Argentinosaurus y estimaron su masa corporal en 75-80 t; al utilizar la nueva información anatómica proporcionada por Dreadnoughtus y Patagotitan; que son parientes cercanos.

facts.statement: Because the only known specimen is very incompletely preserved, it is impossible to guarantee an exact estimate of its body dimensions until better-preserved specimens are found.
facts.quote: Debido al muy incompleto estado de preservación del único espécimen conocido, simplemente no es posible asegurar un estimado exacto de sus dimensiones corporales, hasta un futuro hallazgo de ejemplares mejor preservados.

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus is estimated to have measured 31 to 37 meters in length and weighed 51 to 77 tonnes, making it a strong contender for the title of the largest land animal ever known.
facts.quote: De momento, sus fósiles han dado estimados que lo vuelven como un fuerte rival para el título del mayor animal terrestre conocido de todos los tiempos, este mediría 31- 37 metros y pesaría unos 51-77 toneladas.

facts.statement: Approximately 70% of the Argentinosaurus skeleton has been found, providing greater accuracy and reliability for its size estimates compared to other giant dinosaurs known from fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: a este titanosaurio se le halló el 70% del esqueleto aproximadamente, lo que otorga mayor exactitud y fiabilidad a los cálculos de sus dimensiones.

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus used its long neck to reach high trees like Araucaria or to browse low-lying vegetation such as ferns and shrubs on the ground.
facts.quote: Utilizaba su largo cuello para alcanzar las palmeras y coníferas de gran altura como la araucaria, o barrer el suelo en busca de helechos y otros arbustos de baja estatura.

facts.statement: Inside its stomach, Argentinosaurus likely ground and crushed vegetation using smooth stones known as gastroliths, as it did not chew its food.
facts.quote: En el interior del éste, la vegetación habría sido molida y destrozada por piedras lisas conocidas como gastrolitos.

facts.statement: It is believed that only a very small number of baby Argentinosaurus would survive to reach adulthood.
facts.quote: Se cree que solo un grupo muy pequeño de crías sobrevivirían hasta llegar a la edad adulta.

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus likely traveled in herds of just over a dozen individuals, including juveniles.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus probablemente viajaba en manadas de poco más que una docena de individuos, incluidos los menores de edad.

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus belongs to the parent group Eutitanosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eutitanosauria

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus lived during the Albian stage of the Cretaceous Period, between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: A more complete giant titanosaur was discovered in Chubut Province, Argentina, in 2014 and identified as Patagotitan mayorum in 2017, challenging Argentinosaurus for the largest land animal title.
facts.quote: Se dio a conocer, el año 2014, el descubrimiento de un nuevo titanosaurio gigante mucho más completo hallado en la Provincia del Chubut, Argentina. En 2017, se identificó como Patagotitan mayorum.
